questions.q: What does COPY INTO actually do?
options: Reads matching files from a stage, parses them with a file format, and inserts the rows into a target table
Creates a new stage automatically
Copies a table's schema to another database
Converts a table into a view
questions.explain: COPY INTO is the statement that ties a stage, a file format, and a target table together to actually move rows in.

questions.q: What happens if you run the exact same COPY INTO statement twice in a row against the same stage?
options: The second run loads no additional rows, because Snowflake tracks which files it already loaded successfully
The table's row count doubles
The second run throws an error and refuses to execute
The stage is automatically deleted
questions.explain: Snowflake keeps load metadata per stage (file name + checksum) for 64 days and skips files it already loaded, so re-running COPY INTO is safe by default.

questions.q: How do you force Snowflake to reload a file it thinks it already loaded?
options: Add FORCE = TRUE to the COPY INTO statement
Drop and recreate the entire database
Rename the target table
There is no way to force a reload
questions.explain: FORCE = TRUE overrides the load-metadata check and reloads files regardless of whether they were already processed.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does increasing warehouse size change about a COPY INTO load?
options: How fast it runs, via more parallel compute — not what gets loaded or how
The file format the load uses
Whether ON_ERROR is respected
The stage the files come from
questions.explain: A bigger warehouse speeds up a load with more parallel compute, but it doesn't change the load's logic or correctness — it's a performance lever, not a fix for a failing load.

questions.q: What is the fastest place to check whether a COPY INTO load succeeded, right when it runs?
options: The COPY INTO result set itself — one row per file, with status and row counts
The Snowflake billing dashboard
The warehouse's auto-suspend setting
The database's schema list
questions.explain: COPY INTO returns a result set with one row per file showing status, rows parsed, rows loaded, and error counts — the first place to check a load's outcome.
